SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology02 / 11
Quick Review

In sociology, a theoretical perspective or theoretical paradigm, is defined as an overall view or image of society

Three major theoretical perspectives:

Structural Functionalism

Conflict Theory

Symbolic Interactionism

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology03 / 11
Quick Review

Structural functionalism:

A __________view of society;

Focuses on functions/dysfunctions of the social structure and its parts

Conflict Theory:

A __________view of society;

Focuses on conflicts between categorical pairs (capitalist vs proletariat; white vs black; men vs women) with competing interests and yet asymmetrical positions/power

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology04 / 11
Symbolic Interactionism

Symbolic interactionism views a society as being composed of interactions among its members, which are based on symbols with meanings.

The philosophy of George Herbert Mead (1863–1931) .

Main idea: one’s personality, preferences, thoughts, and ideas are shaped by and through interaction with others and oneself. The self is in a constant process of interaction.

A distinctively American theoretical tradition that continues to be a major force in sociology today;

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology05 / 11
Symbolic Interactionism

Three tenets:

Human beings act towards things based on the meanings those things have for them;

Such meanings arise out of the interaction of the individual with others;

Interpretation of meanings is influenced by specific context.

A small-scale interactive view of society!

SOC 2010 · Introduction to Sociology06 / 11
Symbolic Interactionism

Symbols: Things (objects, behaviors, language, gesture, person….) we attach meanings;

Labeling: to attach meanings to things.
